research_question: In people with patellofemoral pain syndrome, does exercise therapy (alone or added to a co-intervention) compared with control (no treatment, placebo/sham, waiting list, health educational material, or the co-intervention alone) improve functional ability in the short term (up to 3 months), as measured by knee-function questionnaires such as the Anterior Knee Pain Scale (Kujala), Functional Index Questionnaire, WOMAC or Lysholm score?
treatment_label: Exercise therapy (alone or exercise plus co-intervention)
control_label: Control (no treatment, placebo/sham, waiting list, educational material, or co-intervention alone)
outcome_description: Self-reported functional ability of the knee measured with a validated knee-function questionnaire at short-term follow-up (up to approximately 3 months). Preferred instrument is the Anterior Knee Pain Scale (Kujala) when a study reports more than one; otherwise the Functional Index Questionnaire (FIQ), WOMAC (function subscale or total), Lysholm score, or an equivalent patient-reported knee-function measure.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (or SMD) means exercise therapy produced better functional ability (greater self-reported knee function / less functional limitation) than the control condition.
search_queries: exercise therapy patellofemoral pain syndrome randomized controlled trial function
anterior knee pain exercise program trial Kujala Anterior Knee Pain Scale outcome
patellofemoral pain quadriceps strengthening hip exercise controlled trial functional outcome
inclusion_criteria: Participants described as having patellofemoral pain syndrome, anterior knee pain, chondromalacia patellae or similar patellofemoral disorder

Study compares an exercise therapy intervention (alone or added to a co-intervention) with a non-exercise control condition such as no treatment, placebo/sham, waiting list, education, or the co-intervention alone
Reports some quantitative measure of knee function or functional ability (questionnaire score or other functional outcome) allowing computation of an effect size
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a treatment condition and a control condition (e.g. single-arm pre-post study only, or exercise compared only with another active exercise regimen with no control)
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means and SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, odds ratios, or other convertible statistics)

Population or intervention completely unrelated to exercise therapy for patellofemoral/anterior knee pain (e.g. post-surgical knee replacement rehabilitation, ACL reconstruction, knee osteoarthritis only)
moderators_to_extract: Type of control condition (no treatment/waiting list vs placebo/sham vs education vs co-intervention alone)
Exercise type (quadriceps/knee-focused vs hip-and-knee combined vs other)
Supervision and setting (supervised clinic-based vs home-based)
Intervention duration in weeks and total dose
Outcome instrument used (AKPS/Kujala, FIQ, WOMAC, Lysholm, other)
Sample size category and risk-of-bias/allocation concealment
effect_size_note: Pool as standardised mean difference (Hedges g corrected) because studies use different knee-function questionnaires. Sign all effects so that positive favours exercise therapy; reverse-score instruments where higher = worse function (e.g. WOMAC, FIQ versions scored as disability). When a study reports multiple eligible questionnaires, extract the AKPS/Kujala preferentially; use the closest-to-3-month timepoint for short-term follow-up.
